result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers recommend the same variant: Select as the default, Paint as an explicit and visible tool, and Record as a separate button. A goes further on show-time safety: painted lights show their new values, Undo shows how many lights changed, the target cue number is on the Record button, and it argues for keeping cue versions so the operator can undo instead of confirming. B is tighter and gives a frank account of mode errors, but it is less concrete. It also overstates a wrong paint as changing all 48 lights. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers make the same recommendation: Select as the default, Paint as a visible mode, and Record as a separate button rather than a mode. Both explain clearly why the timing-based gestures are risky. B goes further on show-time safety: it shows the mode and the painted values on the grid itself because the operator's eyes are there, counts the lights changed so a runaway drag is obvious, prints the target cue on the Record button, and suggests keeping cue versions instead of a confirm step. B's accessibility and screen-reader points are more generic. A openly admits that modes cause their own errors, but its plan to drop out of Paint after every stroke would slow down an operator who paints repeatedly.
